page_or_component: Homepage - Information Categories grid and Spotlight carousel (india.gov.in, /)
severity: Category tile images and the Spotlight carousel banner images render with the literal word "Loading..." as their accessible name in the rendered DOM extraction (e.g. the Agriculture, Rural & Environment tile and the SMILE spotlight banner both expose "Loading..." instead of a real alt attribute), indicating a lazy-load placeholder alt that is never swapped for descriptive text once the image loads.
user_impact: Screen reader and switch-device users hear "Loading, image, link" for every one of the 18 category tiles and 5 carousel banners with no indication of what each links to, forcing them to open every link blind to find the one they want.
recommended_fix: Set the final descriptive alt text (already present in the visible /heading text next to each image, e.g. "Agriculture, Rural & Environment") on the <img> tag itself at markup time, or update it via the same JS callback that swaps the placeholder image src once the real asset loads, not just visually.

page_or_component: Homepage - hero quote block, search panel, and footer 'Content Sources' links (india.gov.in, /)
evidence: Both the search overlay panel and the hero pull-quote ("India's Digital Public Infrastructure has demonstrated...") and the footer "Content Sources" / "India Portal 2.0 Brochure" links each appear twice, back-to-back, with identical text and identical hrefs in the fetched page content -- consistent with separate mobile and desktop DOM copies toggled by CSS display rather than a single responsive layout.
user_impact: Screen reader users navigating by heading or link list hear every duplicated block twice with no way to tell the copies apart, roughly doubling the effort to skim the page and making the "list of links" navigation mode confusing and untrustworthy.
recommended_fix: Render each responsive section once and restyle it with CSS (flexbox/grid reflow or a hamburger-toggled panel using aria-hidden/aria-expanded) instead of duplicating markup for different breakpoints; if a temporary duplicate is unavoidable, mark the hidden copy aria-hidden="true" and inert.

page_or_component: Site-wide 'View All' links (Online Services, Information Categories, News, Spotlight, Explore India, MyGov Connect sections)
evidence: At least seven distinct links across the homepage share the exact visible text "View All" (pointing to /services, /category, /news/news-on-air, /spotlight, /explore-india, /mygov-activities, /calendar respectively), with no distinguishing accessible name.
user_impact: Screen readers offer a 'jump to next link' and 'list all links' mode that reads link text out of visual context; a user in that mode hears "View All" seven times in a row with no way to know which one leads to Government Schemes versus Explore India versus News.
recommended_fix: Add a visually-hidden suffix or aria-label so each link's accessible name states its destination, e.g. aria-label="View all Information Categories" / "View all Spotlight stories", instead of relying on surrounding visual layout to supply context.

page_or_component: Homepage section headings (Online Services, Government Schemes, News/Press Release, Explore India, MyGov Connect)
wcag_reference: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / 2.4.6 Headings and Labels
evidence: The fetched page marks "Online Services" as a top-level (#) heading in the middle of the document while every other homepage section of equal visual weight (Government Schemes, News/Press Release, Explore India, MyGov Connect) is marked one level down (##), and no single H1 clearly precedes the main content region.
user_impact: Screen reader and voice-control users who jump page structure by heading level get an inconsistent map of the page -- one mid-page section outranks sections around it with no visual or semantic reason, making it harder to build an accurate mental model of the page via headings alone.
recommended_fix: Establish one H1 for the page's main content landmark, then keep every homepage section at a single consistent level (all H2), reserving H3 for sub-items within a section such as individual scheme or news cards.

page_or_component: Homepage search widget - 'Change Input to Keyboard' / 'Change Input to Phonetic' virtual keyboard toggle
evidence: The search bar exposes a custom virtual on-screen keyboard toggle ("Change Input to Keyboard", "Change Input to Phonetic") layered over a native search input; custom virtual-keyboard widgets are a well-documented keyboard-trap risk because focus has to be manually managed between the overlay and the underlying input, and this cannot be confirmed safe from markup alone.
user_impact: Keyboard-only users who are not using a mouse can become stuck inside the virtual keyboard overlay with no way to Tab or Escape back to the main page, blocking them from completing a search or from reaching anything else on the site.
recommended_fix: Manually test this control with keyboard only (Tab, Shift+Tab, Escape) to confirm focus can always move in and back out; if it cannot, wrap the overlay with a documented focus trap that returns focus to the search input on Escape and on selection.
